text: {"frames":["In the Tower corridor the lady in the old portrait has turned her head toward you, and her finger points at the round clock above the stairs. The frame beside her is empty, and a thread hangs from her cuff like a tassel. The little door at the end of the corridor stays shut until the clock is read. What time does the clock in the picture show, in hours and minutes?","The brass key has gone from its hook beside the stairs, and the stairs still climb to a floor that is not on the plan. Anke searches the lamp room and finds only a scrap of paper with a clock drawn on it. Beneath the drawing someone has written that the upper door opens at the right time. What time does the clock in the picture show, in hours and minutes?","Please help us, a small voice calls from behind the map that was pinned to the floor door overnight. Nobody remembers putting it there, and the paper is still warm from the lamp. In one corner a clock has been drawn, with its hands pointing somewhere. Bas can only lift the latch once the drawing is read properly. What time does the clock in the picture show, in hours and minutes?","A smell of wet wool and herring drifts up the stairs, and somewhere a bell hums very low. On the canal below, a barge lantern burns blue and bobs slowly toward the Tower door. Joop follows it along the wet planks and stops at a wall with a clock painted on it. The lantern will only turn off when the painted hands show the right time. What time does the clock in the picture show, in hours and minutes?","This morning the canal runs backwards, and the boats drift uphill past the windmill as if nothing were wrong. The water has left a wet line on the wall of the lock house, and a clock hangs there with its face turned toward the canal. Thijs points at it and says the locks will only swing back once someone reads it. Nobody else in the Tower seems to know what to do. What time does the clock in the picture show, in hours and minutes?"]}
